 80 | @dataclass
 81 | class TaskExecution:
 82 |     """Data class for task execution tracking."""
 83 |     task_id: str
 84 |     status: TaskStatus
 85 |     start_time: Optional[datetime] = None
 86 |     end_time: Optional[datetime] = None
 87 |     retry_count: int = 0
 88 |     last_error: Optional[str] = None
 89 |     result: Any = None
 90 | 
 91 | 
 92 | class CentralScheduler:
 93 |     """
 94 |     Central Scheduler for orchestrating airdrop-related tasks.
 95 | 
 96 |     This class provides comprehensive task scheduling capabilities with:
 97 |     - APScheduler integration for flexible scheduling
 98 |     - DAG-based dependency management
 99 |     - Market condition awareness
100 |     - Retry logic with exponential backoff
101 |     - Priority-based task execution
102 | 
103 |     Example:
104 |         >>> scheduler = CentralScheduler()
105 |         >>> scheduler.add_job(
106 |         ...     task_id="daily_bridge",
107 |         ...     func=bridge_eth_to_scroll,
108 |         ...     trigger="cron",
109 |         ...     hour=10,
110 |         ...     minute=0
111 |         ... )
112 |         >>> scheduler.start()
113 |     """
114 | 
115 |     def __init__(self, config: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None):
116 |         """
117 |         Initialize the Central Scheduler.
118 | 
119 |         Args:
120 |             config: Optional configuration dictionary
121 |         """
122 |         self.config = config or {}
123 |         self._scheduler: Optional[BlockingScheduler] = None
124 |         self._task_definitions: Dict[str, TaskDefinition] = {}
125 |         self._task_executions: Dict[str, TaskExecution] = {}
126 |         self._running = False
127 | 
128 |         # Configuration with defaults
129 |         self.max_retries = self.config.get("scheduler", {}).get("max_retries", 3)
130 |         self.retry_delay = self.config.get("scheduler", {}).get(
131 |             "retry_delay", 60.0
132 |         )
133 |         self._max_concurrent_jobs = self.config.get("scheduler", {}).get(
134 |             "max_concurrent_tasks", 5
135 |         )
136 | 
137 |         logger.info("CentralScheduler initialized with config: %s", self.config)
138 | 
139 |     def add_job(
140 |         self,
141 |         task_id: str,
142 |         func: Callable[..., Any],
143 |         trigger: str = "cron",
144 |         args: Tuple[Any, ...] = (),
145 |         kwargs: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None,
146 |         priority: TaskPriority = TaskPriority.NORMAL,
147 |         dependencies: Optional[Set[str]] = None,
148 |         max_retries: Optional[int] = None,
149 |         **trigger_kwargs: Any
150 |     ) -> None:
151 |         """
152 |         Add a new job to the scheduler.
153 | 
154 |         Args:
155 |             task_id: Unique identifier for the task
156 |             func: Function to execute
157 |             trigger: Trigger type ("cron", "date", "interval")
158 |             args: Positional arguments for the function
159 |             kwargs: Keyword arguments for the function
160 |             priority: Task priority level
161 |             dependencies: Set of task IDs this task depends on
162 |             max_retries: Maximum number of retry attempts
163 |             **trigger_kwargs: Additional trigger configuration
164 | 
165 |         Example:
166 |             >>> scheduler.add_job(
167 |             ...     "daily_bridge",
168 |             ...     bridge_eth_to_scroll,
169 |             ...     trigger="cron",
170 |             ...     hour=10,
171 |             ...     minute=0,
172 |             ...     args=(100,),
173 |             ...     kwargs={"slippage": 0.01}
174 |             ... )
175 |         """
176 |         if not self._scheduler:
177 |             raise RuntimeError("Scheduler not initialized. Call start() first.")
178 | 
179 |         if task_id in self._task_definitions:
180 |             raise ValueError(f"Task {task_id} already exists")
181 | 
182 |         # Create task definition
183 |         task_def = TaskDefinition(
184 |             task_id=task_id,
185 |             func=func,
186 |             args=args,
187 |             kwargs=kwargs or {},
188 |             priority=priority,
189 |             dependencies=dependencies or set(),
190 |             max_retries=max_retries or self.max_retries
191 |         )
192 | 
193 |         # Validate dependencies
194 |         self._validate_dependencies(task_def)
195 | 
196 |         # Create appropriate trigger
197 |         trigger_obj = self._create_trigger(trigger, **trigger_kwargs)
198 | 
199 |         # Add job to APScheduler
200 |         if self._scheduler is not None:
201 |             self._scheduler.add_job(
202 |                 func=self._execute_task_wrapper,
203 |                 trigger=trigger_obj,
204 |                 args=(task_id,),
205 |                 id=task_id,
206 |                 max_instances=1,
207 |                 replace_existing=True
208 |             )
209 | 
210 |         # Store task definition
211 |         self._task_definitions[task_id] = task_def
212 |         self._task_executions[task_id] = TaskExecution(
213 |             task_id=task_id,
214 |             status=TaskStatus.PENDING
215 |         )
216 | 
217 |         logger.info("Added job %s with trigger %s", task_id, trigger)
218 | 
219 |     def manage_task_priority(self, task_id: str, new_priority: TaskPriority) -> None:
220 |         """
221 |         Update task priority for dynamic priority management.
222 | 
223 |         Args:
224 |             task_id: Task identifier
225 |             new_priority: New priority level
226 | 
227 |         Example:
228 |             >>> scheduler.manage_task_priority("bridge_task", TaskPriority.HIGH)
229 |         """
230 |         if task_id not in self._task_definitions:
231 |             raise ValueError(f"Task {task_id} not found")
232 | 
233 |         self._task_definitions[task_id].priority = new_priority
234 |         logger.info("Updated priority for task %s to %s", task_id, new_priority)
235 | 
236 |     def manage_task_dependencies(
237 |         self,
238 |         task_id: str,
239 |         dependencies: Set[str]
240 |     ) -> None:
241 |         """
242 |         Update task dependencies for DAG-based dependency management.
243 | 
244 |         Args:
245 |             task_id: Task identifier
246 |             dependencies: Set of task IDs this task depends on
247 | 
248 |         Example:
249 |             >>> scheduler.manage_task_dependencies(
250 |             ...     "swap_task",
251 |             ...     {"bridge_task", "approval_task"}
252 |             ... )
253 |         """
254 |         if task_id not in self._task_definitions:
255 |             raise ValueError(f"Task {task_id} not found")
256 | 
257 |         # Update dependencies
258 |         self._task_definitions[task_id].dependencies = dependencies
259 | 
260 |         # Validate the updated dependency graph
261 |         self._validate_dependencies(self._task_definitions[task_id])
262 | 
263 |         logger.info("Updated dependencies for task %s: %s", task_id, dependencies)
264 | 
265 |     def schedule_dynamically(
266 |         self,
267 |         market_conditions: Dict[str, Any],
268 |         risk_assessment: Dict[str, Any]
269 |     ) -> None:
270 |         """
271 |         Adjust schedules dynamically based on market conditions and risk assessment.
272 | 
273 |         This method integrates with the Risk Management System and Capital
274 |         Allocation Engine to make intelligent scheduling decisions.
275 | 
276 |         Args:
277 |             market_conditions: Current market data (gas prices, volatility, etc.)
278 |             risk_assessment: Risk assessment from RiskManager
279 | 
280 |         Example:
281 |             >>> market_data = {"gas_price": 50, "volatility": "high"}
282 |             >>> risk_data = {"circuit_breaker": False, "risk_score": 0.3}
283 |             >>> scheduler.schedule_dynamically(market_data, risk_data)
284 |         """
285 |         gas_price = market_conditions.get("gas_price", 0)
286 |         volatility = market_conditions.get("volatility", "normal")
287 |         circuit_breaker = risk_assessment.get("circuit_breaker", False)
288 | 
289 |         # Implement dynamic scheduling logic
290 |         if circuit_breaker:
291 |             logger.warning("Circuit breaker active - pausing all tasks")
292 |             self._pause_all_tasks()
293 |             return
294 | 
295 |         if gas_price > self.config.get("max_gas_price", 100):
296 |             logger.info("High gas prices detected - delaying non-critical tasks")
297 |             self._delay_low_priority_tasks()
298 | 
299 |         if volatility == "high":
300 |             logger.info("High volatility detected - reducing task frequency")
301 |             self._reduce_task_frequency()
302 | 
303 |         logger.info("Dynamic scheduling adjustment completed")
304 | 
305 |     def handle_task_failure(
306 |         self,
307 |         task_id: str,
308 |         error: Exception,
309 |         execution: TaskExecution
310 |     ) -> bool:
311 |         """
312 |         Handle task failure with exponential backoff retry logic.
313 | 
314 |         Args:
315 |             task_id: Failed task identifier
316 |             error: Exception that caused the failure
317 |             execution: Task execution tracking object
318 | 
319 |         Returns:
320 |             True if task should be retried, False otherwise
321 | 
322 |         Example:
323 |             >>> success = scheduler.handle_task_failure(
324 |             ...     "bridge_task",
325 |             ...     ConnectionError("RPC timeout"),
326 |             ...     execution_obj
327 |             ... )
328 |         """
329 |         task_def = self._task_definitions.get(task_id)
330 |         if not task_def:
331 |             logger.error("Task definition not found for %s", task_id)
332 |             return False
333 | 
334 |         execution.retry_count += 1
335 |         execution.last_error = str(error)
336 |         execution.status = TaskStatus.FAILED
337 | 
338 |         if execution.retry_count >= task_def.max_retries:
339 |             logger.error(
340 |                 "Task %s failed permanently after %d retries: %s",
341 |                 task_id, execution.retry_count, error
342 |             )
343 |             return False
344 | 
345 |         # Calculate exponential backoff delay
346 |         delay = task_def.retry_delay * (2 ** (execution.retry_count - 1))
347 | 
348 |         # Add jitter to prevent thundering herd
349 |         jitter = delay * 0.1 * (time.time() % 1)
350 |         total_delay = delay + jitter
351 | 
352 |         logger.warning(
353 |             "Task %s failed (attempt %d/%d), retrying in %.1f seconds: %s",
354 |             task_id, execution.retry_count, task_def.max_retries, total_delay, error
355 |         )
356 | 
357 |         execution.status = TaskStatus.RETRYING
358 | 
359 |         # Schedule retry
360 |         retry_time = datetime.now() + timedelta(seconds=total_delay)
361 |         if DateTrigger is None:
362 |             logger.error("APScheduler not available, cannot schedule retry")
363 |             return False
364 | 
365 |         if self._scheduler is not None:
366 |             self._scheduler.add_job(
367 |                 func=self._execute_task_wrapper,
368 |                 trigger=DateTrigger(run_date=retry_time),
369 |                 args=(task_id,),
370 |                 id=f"{task_id}_retry_{execution.retry_count}",
371 |                 replace_existing=True
372 |             )
373 | 
374 |         return True
375 | 
376 |     def start(self) -> None:
377 |         """
378 |         Initialize and start the APScheduler.
379 | 
380 |         Example:
381 |             >>> scheduler = CentralScheduler()
382 |             >>> scheduler.start()
383 |         """
384 |         if self._running:
385 |             logger.warning("Scheduler is already running")
386 |             return
387 | 
388 |         if not BlockingScheduler:
389 |             raise ImportError(
390 |                 "APScheduler not available. Install with: pip install apscheduler"
391 |             )
392 | 
393 |         self._scheduler = BlockingScheduler()
394 |         self._running = True
395 | 
396 |         logger.info("CentralScheduler started successfully")
397 | 
398 |     def stop(self) -> None:
399 |         """
400 |         Gracefully shut down the scheduler.
401 | 
402 |         Example:
403 |             >>> scheduler.stop()
404 |         """
405 |         if not self._running:
406 |             logger.warning("Scheduler is not running")
407 |             return
408 | 
409 |         if self._scheduler:
410 |             self._scheduler.shutdown(wait=True)
411 |             self._scheduler = None
412 | 
413 |         self._running = False
414 |         logger.info("CentralScheduler stopped gracefully")
415 | 
416 |     def _execute_task_wrapper(self, task_id: str) -> Any:
417 |         """Execute a task with proper error handling and tracking."""
418 |         execution = self._task_executions.get(task_id)
419 |         task_def = self._task_definitions.get(task_id)
420 | 
421 |         if not execution or not task_def:
422 |             logger.error("Task or execution not found: %s", task_id)
423 |             return None
424 | 
425 |         # Check dependencies
426 |         if not self._check_dependencies(task_id):
427 |             logger.warning("Dependencies not met for task %s", task_id)
428 |             return None
429 | 
430 |         execution.status = TaskStatus.RUNNING
431 |         execution.start_time = datetime.now()
432 | 
433 |         try:
434 |             logger.info("Executing task %s", task_id)
435 |             result = task_def.func(*task_def.args, **(task_def.kwargs or {}))
436 | 
437 |             execution.status = TaskStatus.COMPLETED
438 |             execution.end_time = datetime.now()
439 |             execution.result = result
440 | 
441 |             logger.info("Task %s completed successfully", task_id)
442 |             return result
443 | 
444 |         except Exception as error:
445 |             logger.error("Task %s failed: %s", task_id, error)
446 |             self.handle_task_failure(task_id, error, execution)
447 |             raise
448 | 
449 |     def _validate_dependencies(self, task_def: TaskDefinition) -> None:
450 |         """Validate task dependencies to prevent cycles."""
451 |         # Simple cycle detection - can be enhanced for complex DAGs
452 |         visited = set()
453 | 
454 |         def has_cycle(task_id: str) -> bool:
455 |             if task_id in visited:
456 |                 return True
457 |             visited.add(task_id)
458 | 
459 |             task = self._task_definitions.get(task_id)
460 |             if task:
461 |                 for dep in (task.dependencies or set()):
462 |                     if has_cycle(dep):
463 |                         return True
464 |             visited.remove(task_id)
465 |             return False
466 | 
467 |         if has_cycle(task_def.task_id):
468 |             raise ValueError(
469 |                 f"Circular dependency detected for task {task_def.task_id}"
470 |             )
471 | 
472 |     def _create_trigger(self, trigger_type: str, **kwargs: Any) -> Any:
473 |         """Create appropriate trigger object based on type."""
474 |         if CronTrigger is None:
475 |             raise ImportError("APScheduler not available")
476 | 
477 |         if trigger_type == "cron":
478 |             return CronTrigger(**kwargs)
479 |         elif trigger_type == "date":
480 |             return DateTrigger(**kwargs)
481 |         elif trigger_type == "interval":
482 |             return IntervalTrigger(**kwargs)
483 |         else:
484 |             raise ValueError(
485 |                 f"Unsupported trigger type: {trigger_type}"
486 |             )
487 | 
488 |     def _check_dependencies(self, task_id: str) -> bool:
489 |         """Check if all dependencies for a task are completed."""
490 |         task_def = self._task_definitions.get(task_id)
491 |         if not task_def:
492 |             return False
493 | 
494 |         for dep_id in (task_def.dependencies or set()):
495 |             dep_execution = self._task_executions.get(dep_id)
496 |             if not dep_execution or dep_execution.status != TaskStatus.COMPLETED:
497 |                 return False
498 | 
499 |         return True

517 |     def _resolve_dependencies(self, task_graph: Dict[str, Dict[str, Any]]) -> List[str]:
518 |         """
519 |         Resolve task dependencies using a topological sort.
520 |         Returns a list of task IDs in a valid execution order.
521 |         """
522 |         in_degree: Dict[str, int] = {task_id: 0 for task_id in task_graph}
523 |         adj_list: Dict[str, List[str]] = {task_id: [] for task_id in task_graph}
524 | 
525 |         for task_id, task_info in task_graph.items():
526 |             for dep_id in task_info.get("dependencies", []):
527 |                 adj_list[dep_id].append(task_id)
528 |                 in_degree[task_id] += 1
529 | 
530 |         queue: List[str] = [
531 |             task_id for task_id, degree in in_degree.items() if degree == 0
532 |         ]
533 |         topological_order: List[str] = []
534 | 
535 |         while queue:
536 |             current_task_id = queue.pop(0)
537 |             topological_order.append(current_task_id)
538 | 
539 |             for neighbor_task_id in adj_list[current_task_id]:
540 |                 in_degree[neighbor_task_id] -= 1
541 |                 if in_degree[neighbor_task_id] == 0:
542 |                     queue.append(neighbor_task_id)
543 | 
544 |         if len(topological_order) != len(task_graph):
545 |             raise ValueError("Circular dependency detected in task graph.")
546 | 
547 |         logger.debug(f"Resolved dependencies: {topological_order}")
548 |         return topological_order

596 |     def _execute_task(self, task: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
597 |         """
598 |         Execute a single task by dynamically dispatching to the correct protocol module.
599 |         """
600 |         protocol_name = task["protocol"]
601 |         action_name = task["action"]
602 |         task_id = task.get("id", "unknown_task")
603 |         logger.info(
604 |             f"Executing task: {task_id} ({protocol_name}/{action_name})"
605 |         )
606 | 
607 |         try:
608 |             # Dynamically import the protocol module
609 |             protocol_module = importlib.import_module(
610 |                 f"airdrops.protocols.{protocol_name}.{protocol_name}"
611 |             )
612 | 
613 |             # Get the function to execute
614 |             action_func = getattr(protocol_module, action_name)
615 | 
616 |             # Execute the task
617 |             result = action_func(**task.get("params", {}))
618 | 
619 |             # Process result
620 |             success = True
621 |             message = "Task completed successfully"
622 |             tx_hash = "0x" + "0" * 64
623 |             if isinstance(result, tuple):
624 |                 success, tx_hash = result
625 |             elif isinstance(result, str):
626 |                 tx_hash = result
627 | 
628 |             return {
629 |                 "success": success,
630 |                 "message": message,
631 |                 "tx_hash": tx_hash,
632 |                 "error": None,
633 |                 "protocol": protocol_name,
634 |                 "action": action_name,
635 |                 "wallet": task.get("wallet"),
636 |                 "id": task_id,
637 |             }
638 | 
639 |         except (ModuleNotFoundError, AttributeError) as e:
640 |             error_message = f"Could not find action '{action_name}' in protocol"
641 |             f" '{protocol_name}': {e}"
642 |             logger.error(error_message)
643 |             return {
644 |                 "success": False,
645 |                 "message": error_message,
646 |                 "tx_hash": None,
647 |                 "error": str(e),
648 |                 "protocol": protocol_name,
649 |                 "action": action_name,
650 |                 "wallet": task.get("wallet"),
651 |                 "id": task_id,
652 |             }
653 |         except Exception as e:
654 |             error_message = (
655 |                 f"An unexpected error occurred during task execution: {e}"
656 |             )
657 |             logger.error(error_message, exc_info=True)
658 |             return {
659 |                 "success": False,
660 |                 "message": error_message,
661 |                 "tx_hash": None,
662 |                 "error": str(e),
663 |                 "protocol": protocol_name,
664 |                 "action": action_name,
665 |                 "wallet": task.get("wallet"),
666 |                 "id": task_id,
667 |             }

698 | def main() -> None:
699 |     """Main entry point for the scheduler bot."""
700 |     parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Central Scheduler Bot")
701 |     parser.add_argument("--once", action="store_true", help="Run once and exit")
702 |     parser.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true", help="Dry run mode")
703 |     parser.add_argument("--config", help="Configuration file path")
704 | 
705 |     args = parser.parse_args()
706 | 
707 |     # Configure logging
708 |     logging.basicConfig(
709 |         level=logging.INFO,
710 |         format="%(asctime)s - %(name)s - %(levelname)s - %(message)s"
711 |     )
712 | 
713 |     try:
714 |         scheduler = CentralScheduler()
715 | 
716 |         if args.dry_run:
717 |             logger.info("Dry run mode - scheduler initialized but not started")
718 |             return
719 | 
720 |         scheduler.start()
721 | 
722 |         if args.once:
723 |             logger.info("Running once and exiting")
724 |             scheduler.stop()
725 |         else:
726 |             logger.info("Scheduler running. Press Ctrl+C to stop.")
727 |             try:
728 |                 while True:
729 |                     time.sleep(1)
730 |             except KeyboardInterrupt:
731 |                 logger.info("Shutdown signal received")
732 |                 scheduler.stop()
733 | 
734 |     except Exception as error:
735 |         logger.error("Scheduler failed: %s", error)
736 |         sys.exit(1)
737 | 
738 | 
739 | if __name__ == "__main__":
740 |     main()

517 |     def _resolve_dependencies(self, task_graph: Dict[str, Dict[str, Any]]) -> List[str]:
518 |         """
519 |         Resolve task dependencies using a topological sort.
520 |         Returns a list of task IDs in a valid execution order.
521 |         """
522 |         in_degree: Dict[str, int] = {task_id: 0 for task_id in task_graph}
523 |         adj_list: Dict[str, List[str]] = {task_id: [] for task_id in task_graph}
524 | 
525 |         for task_id, task_info in task_graph.items():
526 |             for dep_id in task_info.get("dependencies", []):
527 |                 adj_list[dep_id].append(task_id)
528 |                 in_degree[task_id] += 1
529 | 
530 |         queue: List[str] = [
531 |             task_id for task_id, degree in in_degree.items() if degree == 0
532 |         ]
533 |         topological_order: List[str] = []
534 | 
535 |         while queue:
536 |             current_task_id = queue.pop(0)
537 |             topological_order.append(current_task_id)
538 | 
539 |             for neighbor_task_id in adj_list[current_task_id]:
540 |                 in_degree[neighbor_task_id] -= 1
541 |                 if in_degree[neighbor_task_id] == 0:
542 |                     queue.append(neighbor_task_id)
543 | 
544 |         if len(topological_order) != len(task_graph):
545 |             raise ValueError("Circular dependency detected in task graph.")
546 | 
547 |         logger.debug(f"Resolved dependencies: {topological_order}")
548 |         return topological_order

"""
Central Scheduler implementation for airdrops automation.

This module provides the CentralScheduler class that orchestrates airdrop-related
tasks using APScheduler with DAG-based dependency management, market awareness,
and robust error handling with retry logic.
"""

import logging
import time
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
from typing import Dict, Any, Optional, Callable, Set, Tuple, List
from dataclasses import dataclass
from enum import Enum
import argparse
import importlib
import sys

# APScheduler imports - will be added to dependencies
try:
    from apscheduler.schedulers.blocking import BlockingScheduler
    from apscheduler.triggers.cron import CronTrigger
    from apscheduler.triggers.date import DateTrigger
    from apscheduler.triggers.interval import IntervalTrigger
except ImportError:
    # Graceful fallback for development
    BlockingScheduler = None
    CronTrigger = None
    DateTrigger = None
    IntervalTrigger = None


# Configure logging
logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


class TaskStatus(Enum):
    """Task status enumeration."""
    PENDING = "pending"
    RUNNING = "running"
    COMPLETED = "completed"
    FAILED = "failed"
    RETRYING = "retrying"
    CANCELLED = "cancelled"


class TaskPriority(Enum):
    """Task priority enumeration."""
    LOW = 1
    NORMAL = 2
    HIGH = 3
    CRITICAL = 4


@dataclass
@dataclass
class TaskDefinition:
    """Data class for task definitions."""
    task_id: str
    func: Callable[..., Any]
    args: Tuple[Any, ...] = ()
    kwargs: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None
    priority: TaskPriority = TaskPriority.NORMAL
    dependencies: Optional[Set[str]] = None
    max_retries: int = 3
    retry_delay: float = 60.0
    timeout: Optional[float] = None
    metadata: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        """Initialize default values."""
        if self.kwargs is None:
            self.kwargs = {}
        if self.dependencies is None:
            self.dependencies = set()
        if self.metadata is None:
            self.metadata = {}


@dataclass
class TaskExecution:
    """Data class for task execution tracking."""
    task_id: str
    status: TaskStatus
    start_time: Optional[datetime] = None
    end_time: Optional[datetime] = None
    retry_count: int = 0
    last_error: Optional[str] = None
    result: Any = None


class CentralScheduler:
    """
    Central Scheduler for orchestrating airdrop-related tasks.

    This class provides comprehensive task scheduling capabilities with:
    - APScheduler integration for flexible scheduling
    - DAG-based dependency management
    - Market condition awareness
    - Retry logic with exponential backoff
    - Priority-based task execution

    Example:
        >>> scheduler = CentralScheduler()
        >>> scheduler.add_job(
        ...     task_id="daily_bridge",
        ...     func=bridge_eth_to_scroll,
        ...     trigger="cron",
        ...     hour=10,
        ...     minute=0
        ... )
        >>> scheduler.start()
    """

    def __init__(self, config: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None):
        """
        Initialize the Central Scheduler.

        Args:
            config: Optional configuration dictionary
        """
        self.config = config or {}
        self._scheduler: Optional[BlockingScheduler] = None
        self._task_definitions: Dict[str, TaskDefinition] = {}
        self._task_executions: Dict[str, TaskExecution] = {}
        self._running = False

        # Configuration with defaults
        self.max_retries = self.config.get("scheduler", {}).get("max_retries", 3)
        self.retry_delay = self.config.get("scheduler", {}).get(
            "retry_delay", 60.0
        )
        self._max_concurrent_jobs = self.config.get("scheduler", {}).get(
            "max_concurrent_tasks", 5
        )

        logger.info("CentralScheduler initialized with config: %s", self.config)

    def add_job(
        self,
        task_id: str,
        func: Callable[..., Any],
        trigger: str = "cron",
        args: Tuple[Any, ...] = (),
        kwargs: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None,
        priority: TaskPriority = TaskPriority.NORMAL,
        dependencies: Optional[Set[str]] = None,
        max_retries: Optional[int] = None,
        **trigger_kwargs: Any
    ) -> None:
        """
        Add a new job to the scheduler.

        Args:
            task_id: Unique identifier for the task
            func: Function to execute
            trigger: Trigger type ("cron", "date", "interval")
            args: Positional arguments for the function
            kwargs: Keyword arguments for the function
            priority: Task priority level
            dependencies: Set of task IDs this task depends on
            max_retries: Maximum number of retry attempts
            **trigger_kwargs: Additional trigger configuration

        Example:
            >>> scheduler.add_job(
            ...     "daily_bridge",
            ...     bridge_eth_to_scroll,
            ...     trigger="cron",
            ...     hour=10,
            ...     minute=0,
            ...     args=(100,),
            ...     kwargs={"slippage": 0.01}
            ... )
        """
        if not self._scheduler:
            raise RuntimeError("Scheduler not initialized. Call start() first.")

        if task_id in self._task_definitions:
            raise ValueError(f"Task {task_id} already exists")

        # Create task definition
        task_def = TaskDefinition(
            task_id=task_id,
            func=func,
            args=args,
            kwargs=kwargs or {},
            priority=priority,
            dependencies=dependencies or set(),
            max_retries=max_retries or self.max_retries
        )

        # Validate dependencies
        self._validate_dependencies(task_def)

        # Create appropriate trigger
        trigger_obj = self._create_trigger(trigger, **trigger_kwargs)

        # Add job to APScheduler
        if self._scheduler is not None:
            self._scheduler.add_job(
                func=self._execute_task_wrapper,
                trigger=trigger_obj,
                args=(task_id,),
                id=task_id,
                max_instances=1,
                replace_existing=True
            )

        # Store task definition
        self._task_definitions[task_id] = task_def
        self._task_executions[task_id] = TaskExecution(
            task_id=task_id,
            status=TaskStatus.PENDING
        )

        logger.info("Added job %s with trigger %s", task_id, trigger)

    def manage_task_priority(self, task_id: str, new_priority: TaskPriority) -> None:
        """
        Update task priority for dynamic priority management.

        Args:
            task_id: Task identifier
            new_priority: New priority level

        Example:
            >>> scheduler.manage_task_priority("bridge_task", TaskPriority.HIGH)
        """
        if task_id not in self._task_definitions:
            raise ValueError(f"Task {task_id} not found")

        self._task_definitions[task_id].priority = new_priority
        logger.info("Updated priority for task %s to %s", task_id, new_priority)

    def manage_task_dependencies(
        self,
        task_id: str,
        dependencies: Set[str]
    ) -> None:
        """
        Update task dependencies for DAG-based dependency management.

        Args:
            task_id: Task identifier
            dependencies: Set of task IDs this task depends on

        Example:
            >>> scheduler.manage_task_dependencies(
            ...     "swap_task",
            ...     {"bridge_task", "approval_task"}
            ... )
        """
        if task_id not in self._task_definitions:
            raise ValueError(f"Task {task_id} not found")

        # Update dependencies
        self._task_definitions[task_id].dependencies = dependencies

        # Validate the updated dependency graph
        self._validate_dependencies(self._task_definitions[task_id])

        logger.info("Updated dependencies for task %s: %s", task_id, dependencies)

    def schedule_dynamically(
        self,
        market_conditions: Dict[str, Any],
        risk_assessment: Dict[str, Any]
    ) -> None:
        """
        Adjust schedules dynamically based on market conditions and risk assessment.

        This method integrates with the Risk Management System and Capital
        Allocation Engine to make intelligent scheduling decisions.

        Args:
            market_conditions: Current market data (gas prices, volatility, etc.)
            risk_assessment: Risk assessment from RiskManager

        Example:
            >>> market_data = {"gas_price": 50, "volatility": "high"}
            >>> risk_data = {"circuit_breaker": False, "risk_score": 0.3}
            >>> scheduler.schedule_dynamically(market_data, risk_data)
        """
        gas_price = market_conditions.get("gas_price", 0)
        volatility = market_conditions.get("volatility", "normal")
        circuit_breaker = risk_assessment.get("circuit_breaker", False)

        # Implement dynamic scheduling logic
        if circuit_breaker:
            logger.warning("Circuit breaker active - pausing all tasks")
            self._pause_all_tasks()
            return

        if gas_price > self.config.get("max_gas_price", 100):
            logger.info("High gas prices detected - delaying non-critical tasks")
            self._delay_low_priority_tasks()

        if volatility == "high":
            logger.info("High volatility detected - reducing task frequency")
            self._reduce_task_frequency()

        logger.info("Dynamic scheduling adjustment completed")

    def handle_task_failure(
        self,
        task_id: str,
        error: Exception,
        execution: TaskExecution
    ) -> bool:
        """
        Handle task failure with exponential backoff retry logic.

        Args:
            task_id: Failed task identifier
            error: Exception that caused the failure
            execution: Task execution tracking object

        Returns:
            True if task should be retried, False otherwise

        Example:
            >>> success = scheduler.handle_task_failure(
            ...     "bridge_task",
            ...     ConnectionError("RPC timeout"),
            ...     execution_obj
            ... )
        """
        task_def = self._task_definitions.get(task_id)
        if not task_def:
            logger.error("Task definition not found for %s", task_id)
            return False

        execution.retry_count += 1
        execution.last_error = str(error)
        execution.status = TaskStatus.FAILED

        if execution.retry_count >= task_def.max_retries:
            logger.error(
                "Task %s failed permanently after %d retries: %s",
                task_id, execution.retry_count, error
            )
            return False

        # Calculate exponential backoff delay
        delay = task_def.retry_delay * (2 ** (execution.retry_count - 1))

        # Add jitter to prevent thundering herd
        jitter = delay * 0.1 * (time.time() % 1)
        total_delay = delay + jitter

        logger.warning(
            "Task %s failed (attempt %d/%d), retrying in %.1f seconds: %s",
            task_id, execution.retry_count, task_def.max_retries, total_delay, error
        )

        execution.status = TaskStatus.RETRYING

        # Schedule retry
        retry_time = datetime.now() + timedelta(seconds=total_delay)
        if DateTrigger is None:
            logger.error("APScheduler not available, cannot schedule retry")
            return False

        if self._scheduler is not None:
            self._scheduler.add_job(
                func=self._execute_task_wrapper,
                trigger=DateTrigger(run_date=retry_time),
                args=(task_id,),
                id=f"{task_id}_retry_{execution.retry_count}",
                replace_existing=True
            )

        return True

    def start(self) -> None:
        """
        Initialize and start the APScheduler.

        Example:
            >>> scheduler = CentralScheduler()
            >>> scheduler.start()
        """
        if self._running:
            logger.warning("Scheduler is already running")
            return

        if not BlockingScheduler:
            raise ImportError(
                "APScheduler not available. Install with: pip install apscheduler"
            )

        self._scheduler = BlockingScheduler()
        self._running = True

        logger.info("CentralScheduler started successfully")

    def stop(self) -> None:
        """
        Gracefully shut down the scheduler.

        Example:
            >>> scheduler.stop()
        """
        if not self._running:
            logger.warning("Scheduler is not running")
            return

        if self._scheduler:
            self._scheduler.shutdown(wait=True)
            self._scheduler = None

        self._running = False
        logger.info("CentralScheduler stopped gracefully")

    def _execute_task_wrapper(self, task_id: str) -> Any:
        """Execute a task with proper error handling and tracking."""
        execution = self._task_executions.get(task_id)
        task_def = self._task_definitions.get(task_id)

        if not execution or not task_def:
            logger.error("Task or execution not found: %s", task_id)
            return None

        # Check dependencies
        if not self._check_dependencies(task_id):
            logger.warning("Dependencies not met for task %s", task_id)
            return None

        execution.status = TaskStatus.RUNNING
        execution.start_time = datetime.now()

        try:
            logger.info("Executing task %s", task_id)
            result = task_def.func(*task_def.args, **(task_def.kwargs or {}))

            execution.status = TaskStatus.COMPLETED
            execution.end_time = datetime.now()
            execution.result = result

            logger.info("Task %s completed successfully", task_id)
            return result

        except Exception as error:
            logger.error("Task %s failed: %s", task_id, error)
            self.handle_task_failure(task_id, error, execution)
            raise

    def _validate_dependencies(self, task_def: TaskDefinition) -> None:
        """Validate task dependencies to prevent cycles."""
        # Simple cycle detection - can be enhanced for complex DAGs
        visited = set()

        def has_cycle(task_id: str) -> bool:
            if task_id in visited:
                return True
            visited.add(task_id)

            task = self._task_definitions.get(task_id)
            if task:
                for dep in (task.dependencies or set()):
                    if has_cycle(dep):
                        return True
            visited.remove(task_id)
            return False

        if has_cycle(task_def.task_id):
            raise ValueError(
                f"Circular dependency detected for task {task_def.task_id}"
            )

    def _create_trigger(self, trigger_type: str, **kwargs: Any) -> Any:
        """Create appropriate trigger object based on type."""
        if CronTrigger is None:
            raise ImportError("APScheduler not available")

        if trigger_type == "cron":
            return CronTrigger(**kwargs)
        elif trigger_type == "date":
            return DateTrigger(**kwargs)
        elif trigger_type == "interval":
            return IntervalTrigger(**kwargs)
        else:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Unsupported trigger type: {trigger_type}"
            )

    def _check_dependencies(self, task_id: str) -> bool:
        """Check if all dependencies for a task are completed."""
        task_def = self._task_definitions.get(task_id)
        if not task_def:
            return False

        for dep_id in (task_def.dependencies or set()):
            dep_execution = self._task_executions.get(dep_id)
            if not dep_execution or dep_execution.status != TaskStatus.COMPLETED:
                return False

        return True

    def _pause_all_tasks(self) -> None:
        """Pause all scheduled tasks."""
        if self._scheduler:
            self._scheduler.pause()
            logger.info("All tasks paused")

    def _delay_low_priority_tasks(self) -> None:
        """Delay low priority tasks due to high gas prices."""
        # Implementation for delaying low priority tasks
        logger.info("Low priority tasks delayed due to high gas prices")

    def _reduce_task_frequency(self) -> None:
        """Reduce task frequency during high volatility."""
        # Implementation for reducing task frequency
        logger.info("Task frequency reduced due to high volatility")

    def _resolve_dependencies(self, task_graph: Dict[str, Dict[str, Any]]) -> List[str]:
        """
        Resolve task dependencies using a topological sort.
        Returns a list of task IDs in a valid execution order.
        """
        in_degree: Dict[str, int] = {task_id: 0 for task_id in task_graph}
        adj_list: Dict[str, List[str]] = {task_id: [] for task_id in task_graph}

        for task_id, task_info in task_graph.items():
            for dep_id in task_info.get("dependencies", []):
                adj_list[dep_id].append(task_id)
                in_degree[task_id] += 1

        queue: List[str] = [
            task_id for task_id, degree in in_degree.items() if degree == 0
        ]
        topological_order: List[str] = []

        while queue:
            current_task_id = queue.pop(0)
            topological_order.append(current_task_id)

            for neighbor_task_id in adj_list[current_task_id]:
                in_degree[neighbor_task_id] -= 1
                if in_degree[neighbor_task_id] == 0:
                    queue.append(neighbor_task_id)

        if len(topological_order) != len(task_graph):
            raise ValueError("Circular dependency detected in task graph.")

        logger.debug(f"Resolved dependencies: {topological_order}")
        return topological_order

    def _execute_protocol_task(
        self, protocol_name: str, task_type: str, **kwargs: Any
    ) -> Any:
        """Placeholder for executing a protocol-specific task."""
        logger.info(
            f"Executing protocol task: {protocol_name} - {task_type} with {kwargs}"
        )
        # This would dynamically load and execute the relevant protocol logic
        return f"Executed {protocol_name} {task_type}"

    def _schedule_daily_activities(self) -> None:
        """Placeholder for scheduling daily activities."""
        logger.info("Scheduling daily activities...")
        pass

    def _load_balance_wallets(self) -> None:
        """Placeholder for load balancing wallets."""
        logger.info("Load balancing wallets...")
        pass

    def _enforce_gas_limits(self) -> bool:
        """Placeholder for enforcing gas limits."""
        logger.info("Enforcing gas limits...")
        # For now, always return True to allow execution, or implement actual logic
        # based on self.config.get("risk_management", {}).get(
        # "max_gas_price_gwei"
        # )
        return True

    def _generate_random_delay(
        self, min_delay: float = 1.0, max_delay: float = 5.0
    ) -> float:
        """
        Generate a random delay within a specified range.

        Args:
            min_delay: Minimum delay in seconds.
            max_delay: Maximum delay in seconds.

        Returns:
            A random float representing the delay.
        """
        import random
        return random.uniform(min_delay, max_delay)

    def _execute_task(self, task: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """
        Execute a single task by dynamically dispatching to the correct protocol module.
        """
        protocol_name = task["protocol"]
        action_name = task["action"]
        task_id = task.get("id", "unknown_task")
        logger.info(
            f"Executing task: {task_id} ({protocol_name}/{action_name})"
        )

        try:
            # Dynamically import the protocol module
            protocol_module = importlib.import_module(
                f"airdrops.protocols.{protocol_name}.{protocol_name}"
            )

            # Get the function to execute
            action_func = getattr(protocol_module, action_name)

            # Execute the task
            result = action_func(**task.get("params", {}))

            # Process result
            success = True
            message = "Task completed successfully"
            tx_hash = "0x" + "0" * 64
            if isinstance(result, tuple):
                success, tx_hash = result
            elif isinstance(result, str):
                tx_hash = result

            return {
                "success": success,
                "message": message,
                "tx_hash": tx_hash,
                "error": None,
                "protocol": protocol_name,
                "action": action_name,
                "wallet": task.get("wallet"),
                "id": task_id,
            }

        except (ModuleNotFoundError, AttributeError) as e:
            error_message = f"Could not find action '{action_name}' in protocol"
            f" '{protocol_name}': {e}"
            logger.error(error_message)
            return {
                "success": False,
                "message": error_message,
                "tx_hash": None,
                "error": str(e),
                "protocol": protocol_name,
                "action": action_name,
                "wallet": task.get("wallet"),
                "id": task_id,
            }
        except Exception as e:
            error_message = (
                f"An unexpected error occurred during task execution: {e}"
            )
            logger.error(error_message, exc_info=True)
            return {
                "success": False,
                "message": error_message,
                "tx_hash": None,
                "error": str(e),
                "protocol": protocol_name,
                "action": action_name,
                "wallet": task.get("wallet"),
                "id": task_id,
            }

    def _assign_wallet_for_task(self, task: Dict[str, Any], wallets: List[str]) -> str:
        """
        Assign a wallet to a task, e.g., using round-robin.
        """
        # Simple round-robin assignment for demonstration
        wallet_index = hash(task.get("id", "")) % len(wallets)
        return wallets[wallet_index]

    def _generate_daily_schedule(self) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
        """
        Generate a list of daily tasks based on protocol configurations.
        This is a simplified placeholder.
        """
        daily_tasks = []
        for protocol_name, protocol_config in self.config.get("protocols", {}).items():
            if protocol_config.get("enabled"):
                num_activities = protocol_config.get(
                    "daily_activity_range", [1, 1]
                )[0]  # Use min for simplicity
                for i in range(num_activities):
                    daily_tasks.append({
                        "id": f"{protocol_name}_daily_task_{i}",
                        "protocol": protocol_name,
                        "action": "random_activity",  # Simplified to random activity
                        "wallet": None,  # Will be assigned later
                        "priority": TaskPriority.NORMAL,
                    })
        return daily_tasks


def main() -> None:
    """Main entry point for the scheduler bot."""
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Central Scheduler Bot")
    parser.add_argument(
        "--once", action="store_true", help="Run once and exit"
    )
    parser.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true", help="Dry run mode")
    parser.add_argument("--config", help="Configuration file path")

    args = parser.parse_args()

    # Configure logging
    logging.basicConfig(
        level=logging.INFO,
        format="%(asctime)s - %(name)s - %(levelname)s - %(message)s"
    )

    try:
        scheduler = CentralScheduler()

        if args.dry_run:
            logger.info("Dry run mode - scheduler initialized but not started")
            return

        scheduler.start()

        if args.once:
            logger.info("Running once and exiting")
            scheduler.stop()
        else:
            logger.info("Scheduler running. Press Ctrl+C to stop.")
            try:
                while True:
                    time.sleep(1)
            except KeyboardInterrupt:
                logger.info("Shutdown signal received")
                scheduler.stop()

    except Exception as error:
        logger.error("Scheduler failed: %s", error)
        sys.exit(1)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

 284 |         web3_scroll, pool_address
 285 |     )
 286 |     reserves = pool_contract.functions.getReserves().call()
 287 |     total_supply = pool_contract.functions.totalSupply().call()
 288 |     # Simplified proportional calculation
 289 |     if total_supply == 0:
 290 |         # First liquidity provider
 291 |         min_liquidity = int(
 292 |             (amount_a_desired + amount_b_desired) * (1 - slippage_percent / 100)
 293 |         )
 294 |     else:
 295 |         min_liquidity = int(
 296 |             min(
 297 |                 amount_a_desired * total_supply // reserves[0],
 298 |                 amount_b_desired * total_supply // reserves[1],
 299 |             )
 300 |             * (1 - slippage_percent / 100)
 301 |         )
 302 |     return min_liquidity
 303 | 
 304 | 
 305 | def _calculate_min_amounts_out_scroll(
 306 |     web3_scroll: Web3,
 307 |     pool_address: str,
 308 |     lp_token_amount: int,
 309 |     slippage_percent: float,
 310 | ) -> Tuple[int, int]:
 311 |     """
 312 |     Calculate minimum amounts of tokens to receive when removing liquidity.
 313 | 
 314 |     Args:
 315 |         web3_scroll: Web3 instance.
 316 |         pool_address: Address of the SyncSwap pool.
 317 |         lp_token_amount: Amount of LP tokens to burn.
 318 |         slippage_percent: Allowed slippage percentage.
 319 | 
 320 |     Returns:
 321 |         Tuple of (amount_a_min, amount_b_min).
 322 |     """
 323 |     pool_contract = _get_syncswap_classic_pool_contract_scroll(
 324 |         web3_scroll, pool_address
 325 |     )
 326 |     reserves = pool_contract.functions.getReserves().call()
 327 |     total_supply = pool_contract.functions.totalSupply().call()
 328 |     amount_a_out_expected = lp_token_amount * reserves[0] // total_supply
 329 |     amount_b_out_expected = lp_token_amount * reserves[1] // total_supply
 330 |     amount_a_min = int(amount_a_out_expected * (1 - slippage_percent / 100))
 331 |     amount_b_min = int(amount_b_out_expected * (1 - slippage_percent / 100))
 332 |     return amount_a_min, amount_b_min
 333 | 
 334 | 
 335 | SYNC_SWAP_CLASSIC_POOL_FACTORY_ABI_NAME = "SyncSwapClassicPoolFactory"
 336 | SYNC_SWAP_CLASSIC_POOL_ABI_NAME = "SyncSwapClassicPool"
 337 | 
 338 | # Default gas limits and constants
 339 | DEFAULT_L2_GAS_LIMIT = 200000  # For bridging
 340 | DEFAULT_SWAP_L2_GAS_LIMIT = 600000
 341 | DEFAULT_GAS_MULTIPLIER = 1.2
 342 | MAX_RETRIES = 3
 343 | RETRY_DELAY_SECONDS = 5
 344 | ZERO_ADDRESS = "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000"
 345 | ETH_SYMBOL = "ETH"
 346 | WETH_SYMBOL = "WETH"

 349 | def _load_abi_scroll(contract_name: str) -> Sequence[Dict[str, Any]]:
 350 |     """
 351 |     Load ABI JSON from the abi directory.
 352 | 
 353 |     Args:
 354 |         contract_name: Name of the contract (e.g., 'L1GatewayRouter')
 355 | 
 356 |     Returns:
 357 |         ABI as a list of dictionaries
 358 | 
 359 |     Raises:
 360 |         FileNotFoundError: If ABI file doesn't exist
 361 |         json.JSONDecodeError: If ABI file is invalid JSON
 362 |     """
 363 |     abi_path = Path(__file__).parent / "abi" / f"{contract_name}.json"
 364 |     try:
 365 |         with open(abi_path, "r") as f:
 366 |             return cast(Sequence[Dict[str, Any]], json.load(f))
 367 |     except FileNotFoundError:
 368 |         logger.error(f"ABI file not found: {abi_path}")
 369 |         raise FileNotFoundError(f"ABI file not found: {abi_path}")
 370 |     except json.JSONDecodeError as e:
 371 |         logger.error(f"Invalid JSON in ABI file {abi_path}: {e.msg}")
 372 |         raise json.JSONDecodeError(
 373 |             f"Invalid JSON in ABI file {abi_path}: {e.msg}", e.doc, e.pos
 374 |         )
 375 |

 377 | def _get_account_scroll(private_key: str, web3_instance: Web3) -> LocalAccount:
 378 |     """
 379 |     Create Account object from private key.
 380 | 
 381 |     Args:
 382 |         private_key: Private key string
 383 |         web3_instance: Web3  # (used for potential future validation, currently unused)
 384 | 
 385 |     Returns:
 386 |         Account object
 387 | 
 388 |     Raises:
 389 |         ValueError: If private key is invalid
 390 |     """
 391 |     try:
 392 |         if not private_key.startswith("0x"):
 393 |             private_key = "0x" + private_key
 394 |         account: LocalAccount = Account.from_key(private_key)
 395 |         return account
 396 |     except Exception as e:
 397 |         logger.error(f"Invalid private key provided: {e}")
 398 |         raise ValueError(f"Invalid private key: {e}")

 401 | def _get_l2_token_address_scroll(token_symbol: str) -> str:
 402 |     """
 403 |     Get L2 address for a token symbol from shared config.
 404 | 
 405 |     Args:
 406 |         token_symbol: Token symbol (e.g., "ETH", "WETH", "USDC").
 407 | 
 408 |     Returns:
 409 |         L2 token address as a string.
 410 | 
 411 |     Raises:
 412 |         TokenNotSupportedError: If token symbol is not configured or L2 address
 413 |             is missing.
 414 |     """
 415 |     if token_symbol not in shared_config.SCROLL_TOKEN_ADDRESSES:
 416 |         logger.error(f"Token symbol '{token_symbol}' not found in configuration.")
 417 |         raise TokenNotSupportedError(f"Token symbol '{token_symbol}' not supported.")
 418 |     token_config_entry = shared_config.SCROLL_TOKEN_ADDRESSES[token_symbol]
 419 |     # Cast to Dict to help mypy understand .get() and indexing
 420 |     token_info: Dict[str, Any] = cast(Dict[str, Any], token_config_entry)
 421 |     l2_address = token_info.get("L2")
 422 |     if (
 423 |         l2_address is None and token_symbol != ETH_SYMBOL
 424 |     ):  # ETH L2 is None, handled by WETH
 425 |         logger.error(f"L2 address for token '{token_symbol}' is not configured.")
 426 |         raise TokenNotSupportedError(
 427 |             f"L2 address for token '{token_symbol}' not configured."
 428 |         )
 429 |     # For ETH, we typically use WETH address in contracts
 430 |     if token_symbol == ETH_SYMBOL:
 431 |         weth_config_entry = shared_config.SCROLL_TOKEN_ADDRESSES.get(WETH_SYMBOL)
 432 |         if not weth_config_entry:
 433 |             raise TokenNotSupportedError(
 434 |                 "WETH symbol not found in SCROLL_TOKEN_ADDRESSES."
 435 |             )
 436 |         weth_info: Dict[str, Any] = cast(Dict[str, Any], weth_config_entry)
 437 |         weth_l2 = weth_info.get("L2")
 438 |         if not weth_l2:
 439 |             raise TokenNotSupportedError(
 440 |                 "WETH L2 address not configured, required for ETH operations."
 441 |             )
 442 |         return cast(str, weth_l2)
 443 |     return cast(str, l2_address)
 444 |

 446 | def _get_contract_scroll(
 447 |     web3_instance: Web3, contract_name: str, contract_address: str
 448 | ) -> Contract:
 449 |     """
 450 |     Load ABI and return contract instance.
 451 | 
 452 |     Args:
 453 |         web3_instance: Web3 instance
 454 |         contract_name: Name of contract for ABI loading
 455 |         contract_address: Contract address
 456 | 
 457 |     Returns:
 458 |         Web3 Contract instance
 459 |     """
 460 |     abi = _load_abi_scroll(contract_name)
 461 |     checksum_address = Web3.to_checksum_address(contract_address)
 462 |     return web3_instance.eth.contract(address=checksum_address, abi=abi)
 463 | 
 464 | 
 465 | def _build_and_send_tx_scroll(
 466 |     web3_instance: Web3, private_key: str, tx_params: TxParams
 467 | ) -> str:
 468 |     """
 469 |     Build, sign, send, and wait for a transaction, with retry logic for
 470 |     transient errors.
 471 |     """
 472 |     account = _get_account_scroll(private_key, web3_instance)
 473 |     tx_params.setdefault(
 474 |         "nonce", web3_instance.eth.get_transaction_count(account.address)
 475 |     )
 476 |     tx_params.setdefault("gasPrice", web3_instance.eth.gas_price)
 477 | 
 478 |     if "gas" not in tx_params:
 479 |         try:
 480 |             estimated_gas = web3_instance.eth.estimate_gas(tx_params)
 481 |             tx_params["gas"] = Wei(int(estimated_gas * DEFAULT_GAS_MULTIPLIER))
 482 |             logger.info(f"Estimated gas: {estimated_gas}, using: {tx_params['gas']}")
 483 |         except Exception as e:
 484 |             logger.error(f"Gas estimation failed: {e}, tx_params: {tx_params}")
 485 |             # Include address in log if available
 486 |             from_address = tx_params.get("from", "N/A")
 487 |             to_address = tx_params.get("to", "N/A")
 488 |             # Convert bytes to string if needed for logging
 489 |             from_addr_str = from_address.hex() if isinstance(from_address, bytes) else str(from_address)
 490 |             to_addr_str = to_address.hex() if isinstance(to_address, bytes) else str(to_address)
 491 |             data_present = "data" in tx_params
 492 |             logger.error(
 493 |                 f"Gas estimation failed for tx from {from_addr_str} to {to_addr_str} "
 494 |                 f"(data present: {data_present}): {e!s}"
 495 |             )
 496 |             if isinstance(e, ContractLogicError):  # More specific error
 497 |                 raise GasEstimationError(
 498 |                     f"Gas estimation failed due to contract logic: {e.message} - "
 499 |                     f"Data: {e.data!r}"
 500 |                 )
 501 |             raise GasEstimationError(f"Gas estimation failed: {e}")
 502 | 
 503 |     try:
 504 |         signed = web3_instance.eth.account.sign_transaction(tx_params, private_key)
 505 |     except Exception as e:
 506 |         logger.error(f"Transaction signing failed: {e}")
 507 |         raise TransactionBuildError(f"Transaction signing failed: {e}")
 508 | 
 509 |     last_exception: Optional[Exception] = None
 510 |     for attempt in range(MAX_RETRIES):
 511 |         try:
 512 |             logger.info(
 513 |                 f"Attempt {attempt + 1}/{MAX_RETRIES} to send transaction..."
 514 |             )
 515 |             tx_hash_bytes = web3_instance.eth.send_raw_transaction(
 516 |                 signed.raw_transaction
 517 |             )
 518 |             tx_hash_hex = tx_hash_bytes.hex()
 519 |             logger.info(f"Transaction sent with hash: {tx_hash_hex}")
 520 | 
 521 |             logger.info(f"Waiting for transaction receipt for {tx_hash_hex}...")
 522 |             receipt: TxReceipt = web3_instance.eth.wait_for_transaction_receipt(
 523 |                 tx_hash_bytes, timeout=180
 524 |             )
 525 |             logger.info(f"Transaction receipt received for {tx_hash_hex}")
 526 | 
 527 |             if receipt["status"] != 1:
 528 |                 logger.error(
 529 |                     f"Transaction {tx_hash_hex} reverted. Receipt status: "
 530 |                     f"{receipt['status']}"
 531 |                 )
 532 |                 raise TransactionRevertedError(
 533 |                     f"Transaction {tx_hash_hex} reverted.", receipt=receipt
 534 |                 )
 535 | 
 536 |             logger.info(f"Transaction {tx_hash_hex} successful.")
 537 |             return tx_hash_hex
 538 | 
 539 |         except (ConnectionError, TimeoutError, Timeout) as e:  # Added TimeoutError
 540 |             last_exception = e
 541 |             logger.warning(
 542 |                 f"Attempt {attempt + 1}/{MAX_RETRIES} failed due to RPC/network "
 543 |                 f"issue: {e}. Retrying in {RETRY_DELAY_SECONDS}s..."
 544 |             )
 545 |             time.sleep(RETRY_DELAY_SECONDS)
 546 |             if attempt < MAX_RETRIES - 1:
 547 |                 try:
 548 |                     current_nonce = web3_instance.eth.get_transaction_count(
 549 |                         account.address
 550 |                     )
 551 |                     if current_nonce > cast(int, tx_params["nonce"]):
 552 |                         logger.info(
 553 |                             f"Nonce already used or too low. Current: {current_nonce}, "
 554 |                             f"Tx: {tx_params['nonce']}. Updating nonce."
 555 |                         )
 556 |                         tx_params["nonce"] = current_nonce
 557 |                     else:
 558 |                         logger.info(
 559 |                             f"Nonce {tx_params['nonce']} seems still valid or higher. "
 560 |                             f"Current: {current_nonce}."
 561 |                         )
 562 | 
 563 |                     signed = web3_instance.eth.account.sign_transaction(
 564 |                         tx_params, private_key
 565 |                     )
 566 |                     logger.info(
 567 |                         f"Re-signed transaction with nonce {tx_params['nonce']} "
 568 |                         f"for retry."
 569 |                     )
 570 |                 except Exception as sign_e:
 571 |                     logger.error(
 572 |                         f"Transaction re-signing failed before retry: {sign_e}"
 573 |                     )
 574 |                     # Not raising here, let the outer loop decide if it's max retries
 575 |                     last_exception = TransactionBuildError(
 576 |                         f"Transaction re-signing failed before retry: {sign_e}"
 577 |                     )
 578 |                     break
 579 |         except TransactionRevertedError:
 580 |             raise  # Re-raise if already specific
 581 |         except Exception as e:
 582 |             last_exception = e
 583 |             logger.error(
 584 |                 f"An unexpected error occurred during transaction processing "
 585 |                 f"(attempt {attempt + 1}): {e}"
 586 |             )
 587 |             if attempt < MAX_RETRIES - 1:
 588 |                 time.sleep(RETRY_DELAY_SECONDS)
 589 | 
 590 |     # After loop
 591 |     if last_exception:
 592 |         logger.error(
 593 |             f"All {MAX_RETRIES} attempts failed. Last error: {last_exception}"
 594 |         )
 595 |         if isinstance(last_exception, (ConnectionError, TimeoutError, Timeout)):
 596 |             raise MaxRetriesExceededError(
 597 |                 f"Transaction failed after {MAX_RETRIES} attempts due to "
 598 |                 f"RPC/network issues: {last_exception}"
 599 |             )
 600 |         elif isinstance(last_exception, TransactionRevertedError):
 601 |             raise last_exception
 602 |         elif isinstance(last_exception, TransactionBuildError):
 603 |             raise last_exception
 604 |         else:
 605 |             raise TransactionSendError(
 606 |                 f"Failed to send/confirm transaction after {MAX_RETRIES} retries: "
 607 |                 f"{last_exception}"
 608 |             )
 609 | 
 610 |     # Should ideally not be reached if logic is correct
 611 |     logger.error(
 612 |         "Transaction processing finished in an unexpected state (no success, "
 613 |         "no explicit error after retries)."
 614 |     )
 615 |     raise ScrollBridgeError(
 616 |         "Transaction processing finished in an unexpected state after retries."
 617 |     )
 618 | 
 619 | 
 620 | def _approve_erc20_scroll(
 621 |     web3_scroll: Web3,
 622 |     private_key: str,
 623 |     token_address: str,
 624 |     spender_address: str,
 625 |     amount: int,
 626 | ) -> str:
 627 |     """Approve ERC20 token for spending by a spender on Scroll L2."""
 628 |     logger.info(
 629 |         f"Approving {amount} of token {token_address} for spender {spender_address}"
 630 |     )
 631 |     account = _get_account_scroll(private_key, web3_scroll)
 632 |     contract = _get_contract_scroll(web3_scroll, ERC20_ABI_NAME, token_address)
 633 | 
 634 |     # Check current allowance
 635 |     try:
 636 |         current_allowance = contract.functions.allowance(
 637 |             account.address, spender_address
 638 |         ).call()
 639 |         if current_allowance >= amount:
 640 |             logger.info(
 641 |                 f"Allowance of {current_allowance} for {spender_address} is "
 642 |                 "sufficient. Skipping approval."
 643 |             )
 644 |             return f"existing_approval_sufficient_for_{amount}"
 645 |     except Exception as e:
 646 |         logger.warning(
 647 |             f"Could not check current allowance for {token_address} to "
 648 |             f"{spender_address}: {e}. Proceeding with approval."
 649 |         )
 650 | 
 651 |     tx_dict_approve: TxParams = {
 652 |         "from": account.address,
 653 |         "gasPrice": web3_scroll.eth.gas_price,
 654 |     }
 655 | 
 656 |     try:
 657 |         approve_tx = contract.functions.approve(
 658 |             spender_address, amount
 659 |         ).build_transaction(tx_dict_approve)
 660 |         if "to" not in approve_tx:
 661 |             approve_tx["to"] = token_address
 662 | 
 663 |         logger.info(f"Built approval transaction: {approve_tx}")
 664 |         return _build_and_send_tx_scroll(web3_scroll, private_key, approve_tx)
 665 | 
 666 |     except GasEstimationError as e:
 667 |         logger.error(f"Gas estimation failed for ERC20 approval: {e}")
 668 |         raise ApprovalError(f"ERC20 approval gas estimation failed: {e}") from e
 669 |     except TransactionRevertedError as e:
 670 |         logger.error(f"ERC20 approval transaction reverted: {e.receipt}")
 671 |         raise ApprovalError(
 672 |             f"ERC20 approval failed: {e.args[0]}", receipt=e.receipt
 673 |         ) from e
 674 |     except Exception as e:
 675 |         logger.error(f"ERC20 approval error: {e}")
 676 |         raise ApprovalError(f"ERC20 approval error: {e}") from e
 677 |

 679 | def _estimate_l1_to_l2_message_fee_scroll(
 680 |     web3_l1: Web3, l2_gas_limit: int, l2_gas_price: Optional[int] = None
 681 | ) -> int:
 682 |     """Estimate the L1->L2 message fee using the Scroll L1 Gas Oracle."""
 683 |     try:
 684 |         oracle = _get_contract_scroll(
 685 |             web3_l1,
 686 |             "scroll_l1_gas_oracle",  # This will need to be defined in ABI mapping
 687 |             SCROLL_L1_GAS_ORACLE_ADDRESS
 688 |         )
 689 |         fee = oracle.functions.estimateCrossDomainMessageFee(l2_gas_limit).call()
 690 |         return int(fee)
 691 |     except Exception as e:
 692 |         logger.error(f"Failed to estimate L1->L2 message fee: {e}")
 693 |         raise GasEstimationError(f"Failed to estimate L1->L2 message fee: {e}")

 708 | def _get_syncswap_pool_address_scroll(
 709 |     web3_scroll: Web3, token0_address: str, token1_address: str
 710 | ) -> Optional[str]:
 711 |     """Get pool address for a token pair using SyncSwap Classic Pool Factory."""
 712 |     factory = _get_syncswap_classic_pool_factory_contract_scroll(web3_scroll)
 713 |     try:
 714 |         # Ensure addresses are checksummed for contract calls
 715 |         token0_checksum = Web3.to_checksum_address(token0_address)
 716 |         token1_checksum = Web3.to_checksum_address(token1_address)
 717 | 
 718 |         # Order of tokens might matter for getPool, typically sorted
 719 |         # (token0, token1) = sorted((token0_checksum, token1_checksum))
 720 |         # For SyncSwap, it seems to handle unsorted pairs too. Let's try direct.
 721 |         pool_address_any = factory.functions.getPool(
 722 |             token0_checksum, token1_checksum
 723 |         ).call()
 724 |         pool_address = cast(str, pool_address_any)
 725 |         if pool_address == ZERO_ADDRESS:
 726 |             # Try reverse order if the factory doesn't sort internally
 727 |             pool_address_reversed_any = factory.functions.getPool(
 728 |                 token1_checksum, token0_checksum
 729 |             ).call()
 730 |             pool_address_reversed = cast(str, pool_address_reversed_any)
 731 |             if pool_address_reversed != ZERO_ADDRESS:
 732 |                 # DEBUG: _get_syncswap_pool_address_scroll - pool_address_reversed
 733 |                 return pool_address_reversed
 734 |             logger.info(
 735 |                 f"No SyncSwap Classic pool found for {token0_address} and "
 736 |                 f"{token1_address}"
 737 |             )
 738 |             return None
 739 |         # DEBUG: _get_syncswap_pool_address_scroll - pool_address
 740 |         return pool_address
 741 |     except Exception as e:
 742 |         logger.warning(
 743 |             f"Error getting pool for {token0_address}-{token1_address}: {e}"
 744 |         )
 745 |         return None
 746 |

 763 | 
 764 | def _get_expected_amount_out_syncswap_scroll(
 765 |     web3_scroll: Web3,
 766 |     token_in_address: str,
 767 |     token_out_address: str,
 768 |     amount_in: int,
 769 |     sender_address: str,  # EOA address for the call context
 770 |     weth_address: str,
 771 | ) -> int:
 772 |     """
 773 |     Get the expected output amount for a swap.
 774 |     Tries direct pool, then via WETH if applicable.
 775 |     """
 776 |     logger.info(
 777 |         f"Getting expected amount out for {amount_in} of {token_in_address} to "
 778 |         f"{token_out_address}"
 779 |     )
 780 | 
 781 |     # Try direct pool
 782 |     direct_pool_address = _get_syncswap_pool_address_scroll(
 783 |         web3_scroll, token_in_address, token_out_address
 784 |     )
 785 |     if direct_pool_address:
 786 |         try:
 787 |             pool_contract = _get_syncswap_classic_pool_contract_scroll(
 788 |                 web3_scroll, direct_pool_address
 789 |             )
 790 |             expected_out = pool_contract.functions.getAmountOut(
 791 |                 Web3.to_checksum_address(token_in_address),
 792 |                 amount_in,
 793 |                 Web3.to_checksum_address(sender_address),
 794 |             ).call()
 795 |             # DEBUG: _get_expected_amount_out_syncswap_scroll - expected_out
 796 |             logger.info(
 797 |                 f"Direct pool {direct_pool_address} quote: {expected_out} of "
 798 |                 f"{token_out_address}"
 799 |             )
 800 |             return cast(int, expected_out)
 801 |         except Exception as e:
 802 |             logger.warning(
 803 |                 f"Failed to get quote from direct pool {direct_pool_address}: {e}"
 804 |             )
 805 | 
 806 |     # Try via WETH if token_in and token_out are not WETH and not ETH
 807 |     # (ETH is handled as WETH internally)
 808 |     if token_in_address != weth_address and token_out_address != weth_address:
 809 |         logger.info(f"No direct pool, trying via WETH ({weth_address})")
 810 |         pool1_address = _get_syncswap_pool_address_scroll(
 811 |             web3_scroll, token_in_address, weth_address
 812 |         )
 813 |         pool2_address = _get_syncswap_pool_address_scroll(
 814 |             web3_scroll, weth_address, token_out_address
 815 |         )
 816 | 
 817 |         if pool1_address and pool2_address:
 818 |             try:
 819 |                 pool1_contract = _get_syncswap_classic_pool_contract_scroll(
 820 |                     web3_scroll, pool1_address
 821 |                 )
 822 |                 amount_weth_out = pool1_contract.functions.getAmountOut(
 823 |                     Web3.to_checksum_address(token_in_address),
 824 |                     amount_in,
 825 |                     Web3.to_checksum_address(sender_address),
 826 |                 ).call()
 827 |                 logger.info(
 828 |                     f"Pool1 ({token_in_address}->WETH) quote: {amount_weth_out} WETH"
 829 |                 )
 830 | 
 831 |                 if amount_weth_out == 0:
 832 |                     raise InsufficientLiquidityError(
 833 |                         "First leg of WETH hop (token_in -> WETH) results in 0 output."
 834 |                     )
 835 | 
 836 |                 pool2_contract = _get_syncswap_classic_pool_contract_scroll(
 837 |                     web3_scroll, pool2_address
 838 |                 )
 839 |                 final_amount_out = pool2_contract.functions.getAmountOut(
 840 |                     Web3.to_checksum_address(weth_address),
 841 |                     cast(int, amount_weth_out),
 842 |                     Web3.to_checksum_address(sender_address),
 843 |                 ).call()
 844 |                 # DEBUG: _get_expected_amount_out_syncswap_scroll - final_amount_out
 845 |                 logger.info(
 846 |                     f"Pool2 (WETH->{token_out_address}) quote: {final_amount_out} "
 847 |                     f"{token_out_address}"
 848 |                 )
 849 |                 return cast(int, final_amount_out)
 850 |             except Exception as e:
 851 |                 logger.warning(f"Failed to get quote via WETH hop: {e}")
 852 | 
 853 |     logger.error(
 854 |         f"Could not find a valid path or pool for swapping {token_in_address} to "
 855 |         f"{token_out_address}"
 856 |     )
 857 |     raise InsufficientLiquidityError(
 858 |         f"No liquidity or path found for swapping {token_in_address} to "
 859 |         f"{token_out_address} on SyncSwap."
 860 |     )
 861 | 
 862 | 
 863 | def _calculate_amount_out_min_syncswap_scroll(
 864 |     expected_amount_out: int, slippage_percent: float
 865 | ) -> int:
 866 |     """Calculate the minimum amount_out based on expected_amount_out and slippage."""
 867 |     if not 0 <= slippage_percent <= 100:
 868 |         raise ValueError("Slippage percent must be between 0 and 100.")
 869 |     amount_out_min = int(expected_amount_out * (1 - slippage_percent / 100.0))
 870 |     logger.info(
 871 |         f"Calculated amountOutMin: {amount_out_min} from expected "
 872 |         f"{expected_amount_out} with {slippage_percent}% slippage"
 873 |     )
 874 |     return amount_out_min
 875 |
